assets.prompt:
Use case: product-mockup.
Asset type: industrial design concept board, landscape 3:2, high-resolution.
Primary request: a convincing physical concept for a cube containing 125 individually instrumented fruit-fly chambers, with gentle loading/sorting and modular maintenance. This is speculative laboratory hardware, not an existing validated device.
Style: elegant photorealistic CAD/product-design cutaway rendering with precise but sparse dark technical typography on an off-white studio background; tangible aluminum frame, warm white removable covers, dark optical housings, clear service windows, muted cyan service lines and ochre exhaust lines. No space fantasy.
Composition: one large three-quarter perspective cube centered slightly right, top and one side partially cut away to explain the stack. Exactly FIVE horizontal removable trays; one tray pulled forward far enough that its top clearly displays a FIVE BY FIVE matrix of 25 individual rounded square chamber cartridges. Remaining four trays retained in cube. Small discreet chamber windows, chambers large enough for optical and stimulus hardware around a tiny fly, not a toy cage with oversized insects. All trays have accessible pull handles, keyed docking and service connectors at the back. Neatly grouped tubing at rear, electronics in a separate base. A removable ventilated holding cassette docks on top into a camera-checked single-animal gate and distribution manifold; this is a conceptual sorter, depict smooth passages and clear gates, not needles or suction blasting. A small separate holding cassette stands beside the cube to show loading, with only tiny insect specks.
Show clean leader lines and the exact following large readable labels:
Title: "FLY CUBE / 125"
Subtitle: "Five service trays. Twenty-five chambers per tray."
Callouts: "Removable holding cassette"; "Single-animal gate — concept"; "25 individual chamber cartridges"; "Five sliding service trays"; "Conditioned air + odor"; "Separate exhaust"; "Sensing + ensemble readout".
Bottom small caption: "Concept study • Loading and flight measurement require validation"
Constraints: make the five-by-five tray count visually correct. Each cell has individual hardware mounts and an optical port; the detailed inner sensory components need not be visible at this overall scale. The source holding cassette is not the flight mount. Do not imply automatic tether placement. Air/exhaust are distinct paths. No exposed giant insects, no restrained human, no logos, no fabricated test results, no claim of proven control, no extra text. Professional design-study aesthetic, generous whitespace, legible labels, physically coherent drawers and ports.

Use case: product-mockup.
Asset type: scientific industrial-design concept board, landscape 3:2, high-resolution.
Input image: the earlier FLY CUBE / 125 exterior is a STYLE AND HARDWARE REFERENCE ONLY. Create a new close-up of one of its removable chamber cartridges; do not modify the exterior board.
Primary request: an enlarged three-quarter sectional/exploded view of a single fruit-fly sensing chamber, explaining the actual sensory hardware and movement readout in a coherent small cartridge. This is conceptual hardware, not a validated system.
Style: precise photorealistic CAD rendering with cutaway surfaces and sparse readable dark callouts, off-white studio background, satin aluminum, dark optical housings, warm white covers; muted cyan inlet line and ochre exhaust line matching reference.
Main subject: one small square modular instrument cartridge with rounded corners, a cylindrical interior flight arena, curved surrounding visual-display sectors bearing simple high-contrast vertical bars and a horizon line. Front wall cut away to see inside. A single tiny anatomically recognizable fruit fly is suspended centrally with free wing clearance on a fine schematic support coming from the rear upper rim. The fly is realistically tiny compared with instrument, a small central subject, not huge. Do not depict invasive placement, needles or an attachment procedure. Fly has six legs, one pair of wings shown with a faint motion envelope. The support is explicitly an optional tethered-flight insert whose preparation remains unresolved. A small IR body/head camera in the upper rim looks toward the fly from above and forward. A separate IR illumination diode above and paired optical wing sensors below make a credible top-to-bottom unobstructed optical axis. Offset camera avoids the support. Two small inlet nozzles point gently toward the head without touching; one distinct exhaust opening behind/downstream carries air to separate ochre tubing. A small local near-field sound/air-motion transducer sits in a side recess with a short aperture facing toward the antennae. Include a small removable quiet rest/recovery insert beside the cartridge, with a simple perching surface, clearly an alternate insert not under the fly during measurement. No liquid jets, glowing beams, electrodes, brain probes, or molecules.
Exact labels, set in readable type with clean leader lines:
Title: "ONE CELL / ONE FLY"
Subtitle: "A removable sensory and measurement cartridge"
Callouts: "IR camera • head + body"; "Surround visual display"; "Local sound / air motion"; "Odor inlet"; "Separate exhaust"; "Optical wing measurement"; "Optional flight insert"; "Rest / recovery insert".
Bottom small caption: "Tethered-flight concept • Mounting, calibration and animal care remain open design work"
Constraints: all leaders land on the component they name. Visible input and exhaust are physically separate. Clearly show the paired wing sensors beneath the centered wings and separate camera housing. The sensory ring has small viewports and service gaps, not claimed perfect 360-degree coverage. No concentration, dimensions, rates or biological performance claims. No neural data extraction. Generous whitespace. Product study not science-fiction.
assets.edit_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target: this ONE CELL / ONE FLY scientific product concept board.
Correct only the optical camera geometry. The present IR camera lens points outward at the viewer instead of at the fly. Replace the camera with a small angled camera mounted on the upper left rim, whose lens visibly points diagonally downward and inward toward the central fly's head and body. Keep its support mechanically separate from the central vertical flight-insert support. Update only the existing "IR camera • head + body" leader endpoint to the repositioned camera. An IR camera housing should have one lens, angled toward the fly, with no decorative outward-facing second lens.
Preserve every other element, all typography, all exact labels, fly scale, central support, surround display, optical sensors beneath wings, odor inlet, exhaust, recovery insert, materials, viewpoint and canvas exactly. Do not add components, text, beams, new anatomy or labels. This is a small targeted correction to line of sight.

assets.prompt:
Use case: product-mockup.
Asset type: cinematic speculative product concept scene, landscape 16:9, high-resolution.
Input image: FLY CUBE / 125 exterior board is a DESIGN REFERENCE ONLY. Preserve the recognizable satin-aluminum cube, FIVE stacked service drawers, dark base electronics, clear top loading cassette and muted cyan/ochre service accents. Create an entirely new scene.
Primary request: a gently funny, deadpan scene in a SpaceX-style aerospace mission-control room: an ordinary adult technician casually pours a scoop of tiny fruit flies into the top of this very serious fly-guidance cube as it rests in its command cradle, while rockets and precise landing telemetry fill the background monitors. This is obviously a speculative concept image, not a documentary photograph, and must be labeled as such.
Composition: wide cinematic three-quarter tabletop view. Foreground large cube seated snugly in an engineered brushed-metal command cradle with locator rails, recessed latches, power/data docking connectors and an understated blue status band. Exactly five closed service drawers visible on cube front, matching reference. Technician in plain dark polo shirt and work trousers at left, calm neutral expression, holding one ordinary small clear scoop at the clear top intake. Scoop is inserted through a transparent enclosed transfer hood over the top holding cassette, so the few tiny insect specks travel gently within containment; show no flies escaping the room, no forceful jets, no cruel treatment, no giant flies. Scoop action feels casual and mundane, like loading coffee beans, but the enclosure keeps animals contained. Do not put a second hand on a second scoop.
The room is clean, dark, expensive, sober mission control. Background engineers at consoles are soft-focused; large screens show an approaching vertically landing reusable rocket above a circular ocean landing deck, ordinary altitude/velocity traces and technical camera views. No actual logos or imitation documentary timestamps. Cube and technician are sharp, background monitor glow soft and cinematic; believable practical lighting, gentle warmth on hands and aluminum, blue-black mission-control surroundings.
The cradle front has one clearly readable small display with EXACT text:
"GUIDANCE IS AWAKE"
Beneath that in smaller text:
"CREW INTAKE"
Do not claim an exact loaded count while the technician is still loading.
A tasteful small editorial caption in one lower corner reads EXACTLY:
"SPECULATIVE CONCEPT"
The humor comes entirely from the contrast of routine fly-loading with a solemn launch-control setting. No caricature, no cartoons, no comic text, no grins, no weapons, no aliens, no actual SpaceX trademark. The cube is the same serious modular laboratory instrument, not a glowing sci-fi magic box. Device dimensions are illustrative; do not add specifications or claims of validated operation.
